title: The board is the backlog items in progress
note: board set and done write the backlog item's status through ocoeco; the board shows the items in progress across projects and the latest glimpse. One write instead of two.

title: A board to work by
note: Tasks, states, projects, the conversation, the status bar, selection and editing.

title: Boards as shared data
note: Each project's tasks as a table the observatory harvests.

title: A lock per clone
note: Two jobs working in the same clone at once merged each other's changes; lab-agent should make that impossible - a job declares the clones it works in, and a second job waits for them.

title: Dialogs for half-manual tests
note: A popup that asks a person, whatever the desktop, and waits for the answer.

title: Drivers of every kind
note: oco-agent welcomes any driver: people get a terminal interface (the board, the journal, the inbox, back to back), the author's phone stays a channel, machines use the command line. Today only an AI driver's client is comfortable; by design all are equal. Begun 2026-11-12: the command line any driver can type (oco-agent beat | submit | release | standing | next), answers in plain words. Still to come: the terminal interface for people, and the phone.

title: Stage 4: through ocoeco
note: A finished flow records its glimpse; the board is a view of the backlog in progress and live flows; updates composed from the journal.

title: Instructs any agent
note: lab-agent guide: the living practices from the observatory.

title: A job's header counts only at the top
note: Found 2026-11-12: submit removes every line beginning with '# lab:' anywhere in a script, so a script that carries other text (a workflow, a heredoc) loses lines silently. Only the header's own place - after the shebang - should count. oco-agent's runner must not repeat this.

title: Investigate: the agent stopped starting jobs (2026-11-11, 22:29 CET)
note: The machine was on. The agent started its last job at 22:29:23 CET (while a 21-repository rollout begun at 22:28:30 was still running) and logged nothing more until the author rebooted at 23:14:31, although a job waited from 22:45. The author had unplugged the phone at 22:22 - a clue: some of the lab watches the phone. After the reboot (lingering on) the agent ran but picked up nothing new for about 20 minutes - most likely replaying old jobs, see replay-never. The journals of both boots are on the machine.

title: Stage 3: isolation and resources
note: A git worktree per job; jobs declare what they need; side by side by resource; fencing tokens on shared resources.

title: One shared way for a job to start, check and stop
note: A job prelude: fresh (a branch from GitHub's main, or stop), must (run, stop with a reason on failure), expect (demand a text in an output). Today a diverged clone made a chain stop at its pull while the script went on, writing onto main; land refused - but the job should have stopped first.

title: Jobs on the lab machine
note: Submit, wait, results, preemption - the agent's hands.

title: Jobs in parallel, by resource
note: A long job (a rollout across 21 repositories) holds the lab today; jobs that need different things (the phone, the network, the CPU) run side by side.

title: Stage 2: the journal and flows
note: Jobs as journalled flows of idempotent steps; resume at the next step; the job's own heartbeat with progress.

title: Questions on the observatory's attention view
note: What the agent is blocked on appears in the observatory's waiting-on-a-person column.

title: Never in the way
note: Updates switch over when idle; notifications only when something changed; waits show themselves.

title: A reconnect never replays finished jobs
note: 2026-11-11 23:34: after lab-agent connect (max jobs given as 50), the agent re-ran the session's old jobs - it could not see their results - fifty at a time, on the same repository clones; the author stopped it within minutes. Two replayed pin updates opened pull requests (both legitimate tad 0.4.0 bumps). 1002 jobs were moved to archive/2026-11-11 in the jobs repository and max_parallel set back to 1. A job must run once: the agent keeps its own record of jobs started, never runs a job older than itself unless asked, and connect never resets that. Proven in oco-agent's rules (2026-11-12): run once by construction, and the 2026-11-11 log replayed refuses all 102. Still open until oco-agent, not lab-agent, is the one running jobs.

title: Stage 1: safety first
note: Run once and a start-by deadline; the agent's start as a watermark (nothing older runs unless resumed); connect never resets the journal; the driver's lease and park-on-silence; the outside watcher (a scheduled GitHub workflow alerting the urgent channel on a stale heartbeat); the client's own alarm. Proven by chaos tests: reboot, reconnect, kill mid-job, a silent driver. WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12): the core crate is being added at oco-agent/core (journal, leases, deciding; no dependencies) with chaos tests. NEXT after it lands: the journal kept in tad tables (an adapter), the driver's beats carried from the client, then oco-agent run in shadow beside lab-agent. WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, later): the checks every journal must pass moved into the core (measure), and the journal kept in tad tables (oco-agent/journal-in-tad) is being added, held to them. NEXT after it lands: the driver's beats carried from the client; then oco-agent in shadow beside lab-agent. WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, evening): the journal is kept in tad tables and passes the same measure as the one in memory; the real log of 2026-11-11 replayed through the rules refuses exactly the 102 replayed jobs. NEXT: the driver's beats carried from the client (today the replay takes the driver as present); then oco-agent running in shadow beside lab-agent, deciding without acting, its decisions compared day by day. WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, night): each driver has its own lease; beats are kept in tad tables beside the journal and pass their own check; the replay of 2026-11-11 still refuses the 102. NEXT: the oco-agent program itself (its command line declared with argenv): beat, submit, where things stand, what it would do next; then the shadow run beside lab-agent, with beats taken from the old client's activity. WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, late): the oco-agent program exists (oco-agent/command-line): beat, submit, release, standing, next - its command line declared with argenv, refusals in plain words; it speaks a driver's side and does not yet run jobs. NEXT: the shadow run beside lab-agent (oco-agent mirrors what lab-agent does into its own journal each day and reports where it would have decided differently); then the part that runs jobs, and the watcher outside the machine. WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, late night): the shadow run is installed on the lab (oco-agent-shadow.timer, every ten minutes) and alerts urgently if lab-agent starts what oco-agent would refuse. NEXT (design-heavy): the part of oco-agent that runs jobs (the runner, behind its own port, honouring the journal), and the watcher outside the machine (a scheduled GitHub workflow alerting when the lab's beats go stale). WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, night): the watcher is installed and asked its first probe. NEXT: check the lab answered it; prove the alert path with a marked test; then the runner (oco-agent running jobs itself, behind its own port). WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, small hours): the watcher outside the machine is live and proven. Of stage 1, what remains is the runner: oco-agent running jobs itself, behind its own port, claiming each through the journal - then lab-agent's daemon retires. NEXT: design the runner (worktree per job, the start-by deadline, heartbeats per job). WHERE WE ARE (2026-11-12, early morning): the runner is built and tried for real - jobs that finish, fail and overstay are written down as such; a run killed mid-job (kill -9) is followed by one that parks the job and clears every process carrying its mark. NEXT: intake - taking work from the jobs repository into oco-agent's journal (the listening port) - then the switch: oco-agent runs beside lab-agent on a second jobs folder, then takes over and lab-agent's daemon retires.

title: Stage 5: secrets out of sight
note: A credential helper instead of a token in URLs or arguments; the token rotated.

title: The author's word, linked
note: A glimpse or a decision can name the inbox message that prompted it (prompted_by); the messages stay private in lab-agent, the link is data - why something was done leads back to the author's words.

title: The token is never in a URL
note: 2026-11-11: the process list showed the GitHub token inside git's remote URL (x-access-token in https://...), readable by any local process; it was also pasted into a conversation. Pass it through a credential helper instead, and rotate the token.

title: Progress updates composed from glimpses
note: The info channel's regular update says what was just done (the latest glimpses) and what is being done (items in progress) - nothing extra to type.

title: The voice must not depend on the hands
note: 2026-11-11: with the agent stuck, no alert could reach the author, and the author's messages could not reach the agent - both go through the agent. That night a GitHub issue mentioning the author served (grenudi/lab-machine#23). Better: the client sends urgent alerts straight to ntfy, and something outside the machine notices the agent's silence. 2026-11-12: the watcher outside the machine is installed in grenudi/lab-agent-jobs (oco-agent/watcher): it alerts the urgent channel from GitHub when the lab stops answering. Limits, honestly: a job running longer than 45 minutes looks like silence; GitHub's schedule can run late. NEXT: prove the alert path end to end (a test alert), then lab-machine#23 can close. DONE 2026-11-12: proven end to end with a marked test - the lab answered its first probe in 69 s; a silent probe fired one urgent alert from GitHub, and the recovery was reported. lab-machine#23 closed. Limits recorded in decision 2026-11-12-the-watcher-outside.

title: Every wait records itself
note: Recording is live: every submit --wait and wait appends to waits.jsonl beside the board (when, seconds, --on or unlabelled, the board's current project, the job, how it ended). Next: a gatherer bringing waits into the projects' data, and the observatory's view. Parked 2026-11-12: the lab-agent redesign after the 2026-11-11 incident comes first; resume from the next step above (order: open-commons-observatory decision 2026-11-12-the-redesign-first).
